answer.rationale: The binding constraint this cycle is not cost, it is the 14-day cliff on a non-auto-renewing primary contract while the line runs at 94% of committed volume with no buffer. Every cost-bearing option consumes that clock: negotiate_terms is largely foreclosed because the incumbent has already refused to reopen price, and a failed negotiation leaves no time to land supply; defer_decision (the memory_c5 pattern) worked only because that renewal was explicitly non-critical and fell back to month-to-month terms, neither of which holds here; add_second_source (memory_c3) is the right medium-term hedge but does not answer who supplies the primary volume in 15 days, and qualification lead time exceeds the window. That leaves securing supply, and the guarded form of it: a short bridge renewal rather than the multi-year commitment memory_c6 endorses, so the 18% mandate can be attacked next cycle with the low-cost vendor qualified in parallel rather than under a gun. I am verifying memory_c2 and memory_c6 because they are the two load-bearing claims I would be acting against. memory_c2 is the strongest argument for switching now, and its decisive terms are exactly the ones consolidation strips: 'onboarding was quick' at what volume, for which component class, and with how much inventory buffer standing behind it? If that switch happened with slack in the line, it is not evidence for switching at 94% with none. memory_c6 is the strongest argument for the opposite error, locking in multi-year length to buy price; I need to know whether the volume pricing was won as a term-length trade separate from unit price, in which case a lever may remain open even after the price refusal, or whether it required a concession I would be signing blind. The residual risk is real and I am not hiding it: this decision does not deliver the 18% cut, and it defers the savings obligation into a cycle where it will be harder. I am recording that gap explicitly rather than letting a clean 'renewed, no interruption' entry consolidate into the same shape as memory_c1 and teach the next agent that renewal is the default. memory_c1's stability is two cycles of a different cost environment; it should not be read as a standing recommendation, and the cost mandate remains unmet and open.
